subject: Food Science
title: Fermented Hot Sauce
description: A quick win: understand Fermented Hot Sauce.

hook.text: Tabasco sauce ferments in oak barrels for up to 3 years. That aging creates depth that fresh hot sauce can't match.

buildup.text: Chili peppers are mashed with salt and sealed in barrels. Lactic acid bacteria ferment the sugars, developing complex flavors.

discovery.text: Fermentation mellows the raw heat of capsaicin and develops umami, fruity, and tangy notes absent in unfermented sauce.

twist.text: Sriracha isn't fermented—it's made fresh from chili paste, vinegar, and sugar. Its flavor comes from cooking, not microbes.

climax.text: Gochujang—Korean fermented chili paste—ages for months with meju (soybean starter). It combines spice, sweetness, and deep umami.

punchline.text: Fermented hot sauce trades raw heat for complexity. Time adds flavors fire can't.
